notes: High overlap (80% Jaccard). Both agree that increased MT density data (GFP::TBA-1 intensity and EBP-2::GFP comet frequency) in unc-116 mutants are well-supported, though LLM notes statistical analysis could be improved.

High overlap (75% Jaccard) on in vitro MT bundling claims (C52, C53, C119). Both express uncertainty: LLM questions physiological relevance of NudC requirement; peer reviewers request more quantification. Agreement on need for stronger evidence.

Strong overlap (58.8% Jaccard) on core MT polarity findings (C3, C4, C28, C29, C34, C35, C113-C116). Both find the discovery of kinesin-1's role in dendrite MT orientation well-supported by multiple lines of evidence, though peer reviewers question mechanistic interpretation separately.

Good overlap (58.3% Jaccard) on protein mislocalization claims (C24, C25, C47-C51). LLM finds evidence sufficient despite limited quantification; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN specifically requesting additional quantification to strengthen arguments.

Moderate overlap (50% Jaccard) on separability of MT polarity and dendrite length (C61, C62, C89). LLM finds clear separation demonstrated; peer reviewers uncertain whether dendrite elongation rescue by UNC-116MT was adequately shown, questioning if length defects are due to organelle trafficking rather than MT polarity.

Moderate overlap (41.7% Jaccard) on functional consequences of MT polarity for compartmentalization (C26, C27, C88, C94, C95). Both agree this addresses an important problem and that MT polarity affects protein localization, though peer reviewers wanted more quantification for some markers.

Moderate overlap (40% Jaccard) on KLC dispensability for MT polarity (C65, C66). Both agree that genetic separation of kinesin-1 functions is well-demonstrated, with KLCs required for transport but not MT polarity.

Moderate overlap (33.3% Jaccard) on structure-function analysis (C60, C68-C70). LLM finds differential rescue by UNC-116MT convincingly demonstrates both domains required; peer reviewers uncertain whether C-terminal domain actually binds MTs in C. elegans and request direct binding data.

Low overlap (16.7% Jaccard) on mechanistic model (C6, C76). LLM supports sliding-out model based on MT density data; peer reviewers uncertain about mechanism, proposing alternative model where kinesin-1 moves plus-end-out MTs out rather than minus-end-out MTs in, requesting localization data and clarification.

Low overlap (15.4% Jaccard) on e2310 allele interpretation (C55, C57). LLM supports structure-function conclusions; peer reviewers note inconsistency in describing e2310 as 'partial loss of kinesin activity' when it affects C-terminal MT binding domain, questioning whether this domain affects motor activity.

Claims C44, C45, C46, C58 on TOM-20 localization and cargo transport function appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about validating UNC-116MT transport function.

Claims C2, C13, C14 on mammalian dendrite MT polarity characterization appear only in peer review results. Reviewers explicitly corrected authors' mischaracterization of established literature about mixed polarity in proximal vs plus-end-out in distal mammalian dendrites.
